case_title: O.M. Cherian @ Thankachan v. State of Kerala
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for seven years and to pay a fine of Rs.50,000/-
high_court_outcome: Confirmed the conviction and also the sentence of imprisonment imposed upon all the accused
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleges that the accused, who was married to the victim, subjected her to ill-treatment and torture in their matrimonial home, compelling her to take her own life. The victim had a premature delivery and later became pregnant again in 1993, during which the accused provided her with tablets that resulted in a miscarriage. The victim gave birth to a child who did not survive. On the day scheduled for mediation talks, the victim committed suicide by hanging. The accused was employed as a painter in Delhi and later secured employment in Gulf countries, visiting India only four times between 1988 and 1996. The accused took efforts to mediate the differences, but the victim committed suicide on the day of the scheduled mediation. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 498A and 306 IPC and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for seven years and a fine of Rs.50,000/-, with the sentences ordered to run consecutively. The High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence.
